subject: Computer Networking
title: Self-Healing Networks
description: A micro-lesson that makes Self-Healing Networks usable.

hook.text: A link fails at 2 AM. Nobody wakes up. The network reroutes and logs it. Self-healing in action.

buildup.text: Self-healing combines monitoring, AI, and automated remediation. Detect, identify, fix — all automated.

discovery.text: Runbooks — predefined corrective sequences — run automatically when conditions match.

twist.text: The hard part: knowing when to stop automating and escalate to a human. Guardrails matter.

climax.text: Autonomous networks — minimal human help — are the goal. Not there yet, but the trend is clear.

punchline.text: Self-healing networks fix themselves while you sleep.

quiz.question: What are runbooks in the context of self-healing networks?
options: Predefined automated sequences to fix specific known problems
Physical notebooks kept in the server room
Reports generated after a network outage

details.summary: Self-healing networks automatically detect failures and reroute traffic without human intervention using redundant paths, automated failover protocols, and AI-driven diagnostics.
details.whyItMatters: Manual failure response creates downtime that costs businesses millions. Self-healing capabilities reduce mean time to recovery from hours to seconds for many common failure scenarios.
takeaways: Automated failover reroutes traffic in seconds after failures
AI diagnostics identify and fix root causes without human help
Redundant paths ensure traffic always has an alternative route

faq.question: How do self-healing networks detect failures?
faq.answer: Continuous health monitoring checks link status, latency, packet loss, and device health. BFD detects link failures in milliseconds. AI models identify degradation trends before hard failures occur. When a failure is detected, orchestration systems trigger automated remediation playbooks.

faq.question: Can self-healing fix all network problems?
faq.answer: Self-healing handles common failures like link drops, device reboots, and configuration drift automatically. Complex multi-component failures, design-level issues, and unprecedented scenarios still require human expertise.
